title: 30th Celebration, eight weeks in
headline: Eight weeks in, the 30th Celebration is most of what the list shows.
dek: Since the last File (Nov 3), 36 of the 70 rows on the board's 7-day list were 30th Celebration cards, and one led the list seven mornings running. Pikachu ex 107 went from $249.25 on the Oct 13 list to $35.30 on Nov 6's, down 86%; Pikachu ex 109 from $232.65 to $35.28. Then, since yesterday, Pikachu ex 107 read +26.4% and Espeon ex 108 +27.6%: a bounce, or a day. Every move here is unconfirmed.
why_now: The Oct 8 File said our prices could see the 30th Celebration from day 12, not its launch, and that four of its cards were falling with no checked sale behind them. Eight weeks after the Sep 16 launch the set is 7 of the 10 rows on the list two mornings in a row (Nov 8 and Nov 9), and the first upward moves since Oct 13 showed up on the since-yesterday list this morning. That is the moment to write the whole arc down before it turns.
risk: A 7-day list shows a card only on the mornings it moved enough; between Nov 7 and Nov 9 the two Pikachu promos left it, which means their week-over-week move fell under 5% or failed the rule, not that they recovered. The prices here are TCGplayer's market price on the mornings a card was listed, not a daily series; the start-of-week prices in the table are worked back from the rounded change. A since-yesterday move of +26% on a $35 card is one day on a thin card. Unconfirmed means no sale was checked, not that anything is wrong. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether the bounce holds: if Pikachu ex 107 and Espeon ex 108 are on Tuesday's and Wednesday's since-yesterday lists going up, it was a turn; if they are gone, it was a day. Whether Umbreon ex 110 follows the Pikachus down toward its $35 or stops near $80. The Classic Collection: Lugia went from $211.23 on the Oct 5 list to $132.76 on Nov 7's, and Charizard made the list this morning at $121.26, down 21.6% in a week. And the label: Mission Control is starting to store checked eBay sales for a short list of tracked cards; the morning one of these cards has one, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's 7-day lists published Oct 9 to Nov 9, 2026 (prices Oct 8 to Nov 8), its since-yesterday list of Nov 9, and the Nov 9 list (prices Nov 1 to Nov 8)

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The table: the 30th Celebration cards on the board's Nov 9 list (five of the seven; Mew ex 158/128 and Mewtwo ex 157/128, both down about 24%, are on the board's list below), prices Nov 1 to Nov 8, 2026, the change between 3-day medians at each end; start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, then rounded to the dollar, so within a dollar. The counts: the board's own published 7-day lists, Oct 9 to Nov 9 (git history of data/movers.json), 10 rows a morning, 320 in all, 71 of them 30th Celebration cards; since Nov 3, 36 of 70. The listed price on a morning is TCGplayer's market price as of the day before. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades (its price changed on 3 or more of the last 14 days). A card not on it may have moved less, more, or in a way the rule leaves out. Since-yesterday moves: the board's one-day list, 3% or more, 40% or less without a checked sale. Launch: Sep 16, 2026. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
